subject: Term-sync: MSA exhibit carve & phased capacity ramp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <lchen@skygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2028 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MSA & phased ramp — proposal and ask

Laura — attaching a clean + callouts for the proposed MSA changes and the phased capacity ramp we discussed on Tuesday. TL;DR: shorten the initial term to 12 months with a 6‑month renewal option, reserve the right to add bursts in month 3 and month 6, and add an Exhibit F that lays out the staged seat/throughput ramp and billing cadence.

Can you confirm if the phased billing cadence below will work for procurement? If not, highlight which quarters you need flattened and we'll adjust.

Attachments: SkyGrid_MSA_v3_redline.docx (tracked changes), SkyGrid_OrderForm_PhasedRamp_SKY-8492.pdf

Proposed billing cadence (high level):
- Month 1–3: 25% committed capacity billed monthly
- Month 4–6: 50% committed capacity
- Month 7–12: 100% committed capacity (or as amended)

Next steps I suggest: 1) Laura/CX to review redline, 2) Redwood legal to reconcile carve in Exhibit F, 3) sign once both order form and MSA are aligned. Looping Marissa & Laura B for legal/ops notes.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: (415) 555-0134 | ben.carter@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Chen <lchen@skygrid.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@skygrid.com>, Eric Morales <eric.morales@skygrid.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Jan 2028 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & phased ramp — proposal and ask

Ben — thanks for the draft. Quick read — a few internal flags from procurement:
1) Term length: we prefer a 24‑month minimum or a guaranteed minimum spend for 12 months. Shortening to 12 months will trigger extra approvals.
2) Exhibit F: we need clearer acceptance criteria tied to throughput (p95 latency SLA for inference ops) — procurement + infra will want that.
3) Billing cadence: we can do a stepped ramp but need a single invoice per quarter rather than monthly.

I'm attaching our set of markup comments (separate file) and looping in Eric (infra) and contracts to act as reviewers. Can your legal help reconcile the SLA language and the MSA carve for Exhibit F?

Attachment: (marked up PDF delivered via Drive link)

Laura Chen
VP, Procurement — SkyGrid

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Contracts Team <contracts@skygrid.com>, Laura Chen <lchen@skygrid.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Jan 2028 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft MSA & phased ramp — Redwood legal suggestions

Thanks Laura — welcome the feedback. Ben & I talked internally and asked Laura B to propose language that captures: (a) a 12‑month minimum term with an optional 12‑month extension that triggers at SkyGrid's election, but (b) include a minimum spend guarantee to address your 24‑month concern. That gives SkyGrid flexibility while protecting Redwood economics.

Laura B: see inline proposal below (we've kept it tight to avoid re‑opening warranty/indemnity sections):
- Term: Base Term = 12 months; Renewal Term = 12 months if exercised by Customer within the final 30 days of Base Term.
- Minimum Spend: Customer will commit to $X over the Base Term (to be filled in) with quarterly invoicing.
- Exhibit F (SLA): Redwood proposes a measurable p95 latency SLA; failure credits tied to throughput and observed latency windows.

Aditya: can you confirm capacity availability for the requested ramp (months 4–6 intermediate burst)? We want to avoid capacity shortfalls that would force a fallback model.

Marissa

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <lchen@skygrid.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@skygrid.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 10:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Term-sync: MSA exhibit carve & phased capacity ramp

Laura / team — attaching our redline focused on the minimum spend language and the SLA carve into Exhibit F. Key calls:
1) We kept the Base Term at 12 months but added a Minimum Spend clause (Section 2.3) that satisfies revenue recognition needs. Placeholder amount = $540,000 for the Base Term — open to your number.
2) SLA mechanics in Exhibit F are specific: p95 latency target = 350ms for model inference, measured across rolling 7‑day windows; credits scale by % below target and capped at 30% of that month’s committed invoice.
3) Billing cadence: Redwood accepts quarterly invoicing if the order form includes monthly usage reconciliation statements.

Attachments: SkyGrid_MSA_v3_redline.docx, billing-cadence-table.xlsx

If you agree to the Minimum Spend placeholder, we can prepare the final order form and route to DocuSign. Otherwise, please propose the dollar figure and we’ll send a revised MSA.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Eric Morales <eric.morales@skygrid.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <lchen@skygrid.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@skygrid.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 14:11:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Term-sync: MSA exhibit carve & phased capacity ramp

Laura / Ben — engineering ok with the SLA numbers in principle, but two notes: (1) we need a clause that allows a one‑time grace period for the ramp (up to 14 days) given model warmup and KV cache stabilization; (2) please specify the metric tag for the throughput baseline (we use "inference_tokens_per_minute" internally).

Also, a practical ask: will Redwood provide an early access buffer for month 1 to seed our evaluation workloads (small burst at no charge)? That would accelerate go‑live and reduce rollback risk.

Eric Morales
Head of Engineering — SkyGrid

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <lchen@skygrid.com>, Eric Morales <eric.morales@skygrid.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jan 2028 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Term-sync: MSA exhibit carve & phased capacity ramp

All — great progress. Quick recap and asks so we can close:
- Redwood proposes Minimum Spend = $540,000 for Base Term (we can split into quarterly invoices).
- Exhibit F will include: p95 latency SLA = 350ms; metric name = inference_tokens_per_minute; 14‑day ramp grace period; credits as drafted by Laura B.
- Billing cadence = quarterly invoice + monthly usage reconciliation statement.
- Redwood is willing to provide a one‑time evaluation buffer: a 72‑hour, 2x capacity burst in month 1 at no charge (non‑recurring).

If SkyGrid agrees to the minimum spend placeholder and the evaluation buffer, Laura B will update the MSA and Order Form and we will route to DocuSign (link to follow). Please reply with one sentence approving and we’ll produce final paperwork.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: SkyGrid_OrderForm_PhasedRamp_SKY-8492.pdf
